activation.note: Activation preserves the Bun telemetry-test scope, header and headerless identification routes, adoption gate, and generated-contract alternative. audit.summary: All 27 segments survive at the claimed destinations. The rewrite preserves one conditional identity-assertion obligation, uses only the source adoption waiver, generalizes the application-specific example without changing its lesson, and places genuinely generic strict-disposition policy in the shared node.

segmentChecks.note: The then clause preserves both every-header-URN exact assertion and the at-least-one-URN requirement for headerless telemetry tests; evidence restates both obligations.
The then and verifier_detail clauses require the concrete URN verbatim in a string literal and clarify that it must participate in an assertion.
Prefixes, captured-anything matchers, and comments are all expressly rejected in avoid and verifier_detail.
The why and avoid text compactly retain that an any-call assertion proves emission but not the planned item's identity.
Claimed URNs are defined from Telemetry headers, every one is covered, and comment masking is explicit in evidence and verifier_detail.
This article-only fragment has no standalone knowledge; its sentence is completed by the preserved headerless-test clause.
URN-segment and colocation identification routes and the requirement for at least one concrete URN survive in given, then, evidence, and verifier_detail.
The conditional generated-contract identifier alternative is retained with its 'once generated contracts ship' qualifier.
The shared strict-disposition node preserves strict enforcement, including fail-on-every-finding, no advisory mode, and no ratchet baseline; verifier_detail also names strict disposition.

risks: Headerless scope depends on 'URN segment' and 'colocation', which are not operationally defined in coder-facing text; a weak coder may need the validator or classifier to decide whether such a test is covered.

unobservable: The finding fact: telemetry-test classification by header, URN path segment, or emitter colocation, and extraction of claimed header URNs, requires a new observer.
The change fact: whether telemetry-family adoption is enabled in the repository requires a new observer.
Whether generated contracts have shipped and which contract identifier corresponds to the item is not represented by an observable activation fact.
The file_kind and language facts alone do not independently establish that a TypeScript or JavaScript test specifically uses Bun.

review.summary: The rewrite preserves the exact-URN assertion obligation, headerless fallback, generated-contract alternative, adoption gate, and shared strict-enforcement policy, so I agree with the auditor's PASS. Coder-facing behavior is clear once scope is known, although deterministic activation still needs observers for telemetry-test classification, adoption state, and generated-contract availability.
